title: JSON Query Language — Filter
description: A JSON-encoded, SQL-flavoured predicate language for searching a collection of records. Everything needed to write a correct filter is described here, operator by operator, so this schema can be used directly as the input schema of a search tool an agent calls, or referenced from an OpenAPI document so every search endpoint in an API shares one filter grammar. Normative semantics are defined in SPEC.md.

Filter.title: Filter
Filter.description: A predicate over a record. Sibling members are combined with implicit AND: every member must evaluate TRUE for the filter to match. Keys beginning with '$' are reserved for logical operators; a field whose real name begins with '$' is escaped by doubling it ('$$price' means the field '$price').

$and.title: $and
$and.description: All of the listed filters must evaluate TRUE.

$or.title: $or
$or.description: At least one of the listed filters must evaluate TRUE.

$nor.title: $nor
$nor.description: NOT (a OR b OR …), evaluated under three-valued logic. It is TRUE only when every listed filter is FALSE: if one of them is UNKNOWN the result is UNKNOWN, not TRUE, so a $nor over a nullable field excludes the records whose field is null or absent. See SPEC.md §4.1.

$not.title: $not
$not.description: Negates a filter. Under three-valued logic NOT UNKNOWN is UNKNOWN, not TRUE — so this does not match records whose field is null or absent. Add $unknownAs to the inner constraint to include them. See SPEC.md §4.1.

propertyNames.$comment: Deliberately overlaps with patternProperties/additionalProperties above: those two enforce the default grammar, while this is the single named override point. Narrow #/$defs/FieldPath in a bundled copy of this schema to restrict an endpoint to a fixed field set — the narrowing then applies at every nesting level, because Filter recurses through this same $ref. See README §Restricting the queryable field set.

FieldPath.title: Field path
FieldPath.description: A dotted path to a member of the record: 'a.b.c'. An array element is addressed by index ('items[0]'); to say something about the elements of an array without naming an index, use $some or $every, which quantify explicitly. A literal '.' inside a key is escaped as '\.'. The default rule is permissive — any non-empty string not beginning with a single '$' — because the set of queryable paths is a property of the resource, not of the language. Full grammar in SPEC.md §3.

not.$comment: The '[*]' wildcard was removed in v0.4.0; $some and $every replace it. Rejecting it here turns a stale filter into a validation error instead of a path that would be read as a literal key name.

Constraint.title: Constraint
Constraint.description: The condition applied to one field. Either a scalar shorthand — {"status": "open"} is exactly {"status": {"$eq": "open"}} — or an object of operators. Arrays and objects are deliberately excluded from the shorthand so that {"tags": ["a"]} can never be read ambiguously as either $eq or $in.

ConstraintObject.title: Constraint object
ConstraintObject.description: One or more operators applied to the same field. Sibling operators are combined with implicit AND, so {"age": {"$gt": 18, "$ne": 30}} is a single well-formed constraint.

$unknownAs.$comment: $unknownAs is a modifier, not a predicate: it needs at least one operator to modify. Requiring a second member forbids {"$unknownAs": true} standing alone.

$eq.title: $eq
$eq.description: Field equals the operand. Any JSON value, including null, arrays and objects. A value of a different JSON type is unequal — FALSE, not UNKNOWN.

$ne.title: $ne
$ne.description: Field does not equal the operand. The negation of $eq under three-valued logic, so this is UNKNOWN — and therefore does not match — when the field is null or absent. Add $unknownAs: true to include those records. See SPEC.md §4.1.

$gt.title: $gt
$gt.description: Field is strictly greater than the operand.

$gte.title: $gte
$gte.description: Field is greater than or equal to the operand.

$lt.title: $lt
$lt.description: Field is strictly less than the operand.

$lte.title: $lte
$lte.description: Field is less than or equal to the operand.

$between.title: $between
$between.description: Field falls within [lower, upper], inclusive of both bounds.

$nbetween.title: $nbetween
$nbetween.description: Field falls outside [lower, upper]. The negation of $between under three-valued logic, so it is UNKNOWN when the field is null or absent.

$in.title: $in
$in.description: Field equals at least one member of the list. Compares the whole value — it does NOT test membership inside an array-valued field: {"tags": {"$in": ["a"]}} asks whether tags equals "a". For array elements quantify explicitly: {"tags": {"$some": {"$in": ["a"]}}}.

$nin.title: $nin
$nin.description: Field equals no member of the list. Like $in, compares the whole value rather than array elements. The negation of $in under three-valued logic, so it is UNKNOWN when the field is null or absent.

$like.title: $like
$like.description: SQL LIKE pattern: '%' matches any run of characters, '_' matches exactly one, and '\' escapes either. Case-sensitive.

$nlike.title: $nlike
$nlike.description: Negated $like, under three-valued logic: UNKNOWN when the field is null, absent or not a string.

$ilike.title: $ilike
$ilike.description: Case-insensitive $like. Collation is server-defined; see SPEC.md §5.5.

$nilike.title: $nilike
$nilike.description: Negated $ilike, under three-valued logic: UNKNOWN when the field is null, absent or not a string.

$startsWith.title: $startsWith
$startsWith.description: Field begins with this literal substring. Wildcards are not interpreted.

$endsWith.title: $endsWith
$endsWith.description: Field ends with this literal substring. Wildcards are not interpreted.

$contains.title: $contains
$contains.description: Field contains this literal substring. String-only — for arrays, quantify over the elements with $some or $every.

$regex.title: $regex
$regex.description: Field matches this regular expression (ECMA-262 syntax). Servers SHOULD bound execution time; see SPEC.md §7.

$flags.title: $flags
$flags.description: Modifiers for $regex: 'i' case-insensitive, 'm' multiline, 's' dot-matches-newline. Only valid alongside $regex.

$exists.title: $exists
$exists.description: true if the field is present on the record, even when its value is null; false if absent. Total — never UNKNOWN. Distinct from $isNull — see SPEC.md §4.2.

$isNull.title: $isNull
$isNull.description: true if the field's value is null (equivalent to {"$eq": null}); false if it is non-null (equivalent to {"$ne": null}). UNKNOWN only when the path resolves to nothing.

$type.title: $type
$type.description: Field's JSON type. 'integer' matches a number with no fractional part.

$some.title: $some
$some.description: At least one element of the array-valued field satisfies this condition. Supply a Filter for arrays of objects (paths are relative to the element) or a constraint object for arrays of scalars. An element for which the condition is UNKNOWN does not satisfy it, so the quantifier yields TRUE or FALSE over any array — FALSE for an empty one. It is UNKNOWN only when the field is not an array, including when it is null or absent. See SPEC.md §5.8.

$every.title: $every
$every.description: Every element of the array-valued field satisfies this condition; an element for which it is UNKNOWN does not. TRUE for an empty array, vacuously. UNKNOWN only when the field is not an array, including when it is null or absent — a missing array is not vacuously TRUE. Same operand shape as $some. See SPEC.md §5.8.

$hasAll.title: $hasAll
$hasAll.description: The array-valued field contains every member of this list. Quantifies over the operand rather than over the elements, which is why it is not expressible as a $some or $every. Set semantics: multiplicity is ignored. UNKNOWN when the field is not an array.

$size.title: $size
$size.description: Length of the array-valued field: either an exact count or a nested numeric constraint.

$search.title: $search
$search.description: Free-text match against the field. Tokenisation, stemming and relevance are server-defined.

$not.title: $not (field-level)
$not.description: Negates the constraint on this field. {"age": {"$not": {"$gt": 5}}} is TRUE when age is not greater than 5 and UNKNOWN when age is null or absent.

$unknownAs.title: $unknownAs
$unknownAs.description: Resolves UNKNOWN to TRUE or FALSE for this constraint, applied last — after every sibling operator, including a field-level $not. {"status": {"$ne": "archived", "$unknownAs": true}} means 'not archived, and count the records where status is null or absent'. A modifier, not a predicate: it needs at least one operator beside it. No-op on $exists, which is already total. See SPEC.md §4.6.

Operand.title: Operand
Operand.description: A value to compare against: any JSON value, a reference to another field of the same record, or a $literal-wrapped value.

OrderedOperand.title: Ordered operand
OrderedOperand.description: A value on which an ordering is defined: a number, or a string compared lexicographically — which for RFC 3339 date, date-time and time strings coincides with chronological order.

ValueRef.title: Field reference
ValueRef.description: Compares against another field of the same record rather than a constant: {"price": {"$gt": {"$field": "cost"}}} is SQL's WHERE price > cost.

LiteralWrapper.title: Literal escape
LiteralWrapper.description: Forces the wrapped value to be treated as data. Required only when an object operand would otherwise look like a field reference, e.g. {"$literal": {"$field": "not-a-reference"}}.

PlainValue.title: Plain value
PlainValue.description: Any JSON value that is not an object carrying '$'-prefixed keys. The '$' prefix is reserved for $field and $literal, so plain object operands must not use it.

Bounds.title: Bounds
Bounds.description: An inclusive [lower, upper] pair. Both bounds SHOULD be of the same type.

OperandSet.title: Operand set
OperandSet.description: A non-empty list of distinct values. Servers MAY cap its length; see SPEC.md §7.

SizeConstraint.title: Size constraint
SizeConstraint.description: An exact array length, or a comparison on that length.
